chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Sindi ibn al-Rabi' from Sa'id ibn Janah who said:
I was with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in a house in Medina, and he began by saying: 'For one who completes his ruku', fear will not enter his grave.'

key_terms.وَحْشَه: Fear or loneliness (specifically in the grave)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for completing the ruku' in prayer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the physical completeness of the ruku' to spiritual tranquility, specifically the absence of 'wahshah' (spiritual isolation or fear) in the grave. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *khushu'* (presence of heart) during prayer as a means of securing peace in the intermediate realm (*Barzakh*). The narration underscores that ritual precision is not merely mechanical but serves as a safeguard against the existential dread of death.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakil from Muhammad b. Yahya al-’Attar from Muhammad b. Ahmad from al-Sindi b. al-Rabee’ from Sa’eed b. Janah who said:
“For one who completes his Ruku, fear won’t enter his grave.”
